tier_rationale: A quartz digital watch built on Casio's Module 593 with no radio of any kind — not Bluetooth, not radio-controlled timekeeping. Nothing in it can transmit or receive.
the_unplug_test: It keeps telling you the time. There is no pairing, no account, no app, no charging cable, and no operating system that will one day stop being supported. A single CR2016 cell runs it for a stated seven years, and people routinely get ten. The failure mode is a dead battery, and the fix costs about two dollars.

repairability.notes: Four caseback screws and a standard CR2016 cell. Straps and modules are both replaceable, and the watch is cheap enough that most people replace rather than repair — but it can be repaired.

sources.supports: Module 593 quartz movement, CR2016 cell with stated 7-year life, ±30 seconds/month accuracy, chronograph, alarm, annual calendar and LED backlight. Explicitly no radio, Bluetooth, or smart capability. In production since 1989 and still made.
Independent corroboration of the specification set and of continued current production, with no connectivity features in the model.

open_questions: Manufacturer specification page timed out on fetch; swap the primary source to casio.com when it can be retrieved, to upgrade this record's evidence from two Class B sources to Class A.
Casio sells radio-controlled (Wave Ceptor) and Bluetooth-equipped watches under similar-looking model codes — worth adding a short warning about which prefixes carry radios.
notes: Held to the same bar as everything else despite being obviously radio-free, because 'obviously' is how wrong records get written. The evidence here is two independent Class B sources rather than Class A, and the record says so.

changelog.change: First published at D0 on two Class B sources; Class A pending.
